How Lambda compute primitives compare
What is AWS Lambda?
AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service. With Lambda, you can run code without
    provisioning or managing servers. Lambda automatically manages the underlying
    infrastructure – including server maintenance, capacity provisioning,
    scaling, and patching – so you can focus on your application
    logic.
Lambda provides three compute primitives, each designed for different
    workload patterns:
Lambda
        Event Functions
– Run code in response to events or
        API calls without managing servers. You write a handler function, connect
        it to a trigger (API Gateway, Amazon S3, Amazon SQS, EventBridge, and 200+ other AWS
        services), and Lambda executes it. Each invocation runs independently with
        no shared state, scaling horizontally to match demand. Lambda manages
        execution environments, scaling, routing, and fault tolerance.
Lambda
        Web Functions
– Run web applications and API
        backends as HTTP servers. Your Node.js code listens on a
        port and handles HTTP requests directly, using web frameworks such as
        Express, Hono, or React Router
        without adapters. Each
        execution environment serves multiple concurrent requests. Lambda provides
        an HTTPS endpoint, scales your application based on traffic (including to
        zero), and can replicate it across AWS Regions.
Lambda
        MicroVMs
– Isolated compute environments with
        near-instant startup and a total lifespan of up to 8 hours (including
        both running and suspended time). Designed for
        workloads needing a dedicated compute environment for each individual
        user or job. Lambda manages isolation, capacity, and networking. Your
        application uses Lambda MicroVMs APIs and HTTPS endpoints to connect each
        user/job to their compute environment.
Note
Event Functions
is the name for the original
      Lambda function type that runs your code in response to events and API calls. The name
      distinguishes this function type from
Lambda Web
      Functions
and
Lambda MicroVMs
, and
      the Lambda console labels it
Event function
. The underlying resource
      is unchanged: the API operations (such as
CreateFunction
and
Invoke
), the AWS SDKs, the AWS CLI, the
AWS::Lambda::Function
resource type, and ARNs continue to use
function
, so you don't need to change any code, infrastructure
      templates, or IAM permissions.
For pricing information, see
AWS Lambda Pricing
.
How Lambda compute primitives compare
Lambda Event Functions, Lambda Web Functions, and Lambda MicroVMs share a
      common serverless foundation:
No server management
–
          AWS manages underlying infrastructure, instance patching, and
          capacity.
Pay-per-use billing
–
          No upfront commitments. You pay only for the resources
          used.
Managed networking
– All
          three provide service-managed inbound and outbound network
          access.
Firecracker virtualization
– VM-level isolation between workloads.
While they share this foundation, they serve different use
      cases:
Lambda
              Event Functions
Lambda Web
              Functions
Lambda
              MicroVMs
Best for
Request-response or event-driven workloads (APIs, data
              processing, automation)
Web applications and API backends that serve HTTP traffic
              directly
Persistent environments running user or AI-produced untrusted
              code
Programming model
Function handler invoked in a supported runtime
HTTP server that listens on a port, using standard web
              frameworks
Any application – run your own binaries, listen on
              ports, use Linux OS capabilities
Duration
Up to 15 minutes per invocation by default; up to 90
              minutes per asynchronous or event source mapping invocation on Lambda
              Managed Instances; multi-step
              workflows lasting up to a year with Lambda Durable Functions
Up to 15 minutes per HTTP request (default 30
              seconds)
Up to 8 hours per session; suspend and resume across
              sessions
Runtime environment
Service-provided language runtimes; support for
              customer-provided runtimes
Service-provided Node.js runtimes
Customer-provided MicroVM images
Inbound Networking
Direct invocations or event-source integrations with AWS
              services
Service-provided HTTPS endpoint with TLS; optional
              latency-based routing across AWS Regions
Inbound access to any port using OSI Layer 7
              protocols
Concurrency
One request per execution environment at a time by
              default; multiple concurrent requests per execution environment
              for Lambda Managed Instances
Multiple concurrent requests per execution environment
Multiple concurrent connections per MicroVM
Environment State
Execution environments can be reused (warm starts), but state
              might not persist across invocations
Execution environments can be reused (warm starts), but state
              might not persist across invocations
Memory and disk state preserved on suspend; restored on
              resume
Scaling
Automatic – Lambda creates and destroys execution
              environments in response to traffic
Automatic – Lambda creates and destroys execution
              environments in response to traffic, scaling to zero when
              idle
Developer-controlled – you create, suspend, resume, and
              terminate MicroVMs through the API
Lifecycle
Fully managed by Lambda
Fully managed by Lambda
Developer-controlled; optional idle policies for automatic
              suspend-resume
Pricing
Per-request + GB-seconds of execution time
Per request, plus active CPU time (billed in 1 ms increments) and memory for each
              execution environment's lifetime
Per-second of compute while running + snapshot storage while
              suspended
